title: I built a free cross-platform mech arena game (PC, Android, browser) as a solo dev with Claude Code. Here's what worked and what didn't
author: AlternativeEngine422
selftext:
I'm a solo dev and for the last few weeks I've been building Ironvale, a free top-down mech arena brawler (Unity 6, Netcode + Relay) that runs on Windows, Android and in the browser. Almost all of the code was written with Claude Code (an AI coding agent working inside my project), with me directing, testing and deciding what the game should be. Sharing what that was actually like, since this sub is about exactly that.

**What worked really well**

- **Systems, not snippets.** The agent works across the whole Unity project: it wrote the mech combat, 40+ mechs with unique weapons/dashes/supers, online multiplayer with a host-side anti-cheat referee, bots, ranked, a map creator with share links, and this week an "Evolution" system with multi-island trials you can now play co-op with up to 4 friends (each extra pilot makes the trial harder).
- **Headless builds and self-testing.** When the Unity editor bridge broke, it built Windows/Android/WebGL from the command line and tested its own changes by launching the build with dev flags and screenshotting it. Example: new players said they couldn't find the enemy in the tutorial. It found the bot spawned ~100 m away, moved it to 24 m, added an off-screen red arrow with distance, and verified it with screenshots in both the PC and browser builds.
- **The boring stuff.** Release builds, GitHub releases, the website, a Fandom wiki generated from the game's own data, and even the trailers (rendered from HTML with HyperFrames, AI voice narration) are all done through the same agent.

**What didn't**

- It will happily say "done" for things it can't see, so I made "never claim it works without verifying it" a hard rule. Screenshots and real test runs caught a lot.
- Big refactors can quietly break netcode; online features need a real two-client test every time.
- Taste is still on me. It builds what I describe, so vague ideas give generic results.

**Disclosure:** code, wiki and video narration are AI-assisted (Claude / TTS voice). Gameplay design, direction and testing are mine.

Play free in the browser: https://ironvale.gmicrosystem.com/play/
Devlog: https://arcsteel-reactor-studios.itch.io/ironvale

Happy to answer questions about the workflow, what I'd do differently, or where it struggled.

comments.author: iliadz
comments.body: Initial thoughts...The time to kill is extremely long. Pausing doesn't seem to actually pause the game. Didn't go much more than that, but it looks promising, you just need some tuning. Also they seem to lock on to you pretty easy, and it seems constant.

replies.author: AlternativeEngine422
replies.body: Thanks a lot bro, but the thing is, it's made to like me multi-player including the bots which count as multi-player so like making the menu pause them would kinda be pausing a game mid fight in fortnite, everyone would be stuck and would stay still. I kinda don't know what the time to kill is extremely long means tho but thanks. Would really appreciate if you could give me more advice on what I can tune.

replies.author: iliadz
replies.body:
Then why offer pause? I have a mult-player game I am working on, and it has solo, like yours. If you don't offer pause for multiplayer, don't show that, for single player, allow it. Or remove the option alltogether would be my feedback.  
The time to kill is just way too long. That's one of the tuning I would do. Make it about half thaat from what I can tell. So time to kill literally means, how long it take to kill the bots. Evey game has a time to kill. It might be one shot, two shots, or a hundred.

replies.author: AlternativeEngine422
replies.body: Thanks a lot, I will try adding those changes. Also, my bad about the game paused, I tried to add a thing where players could leave or change settings mid game, that's why.

replies.author: AlternativeEngine422
replies.body: Practically, I launched 2 clients same time to check multi-player worked and if the new features were implemented correctly
